textbookText: A. Tick the correct alternative. 1. Which epoch of the Cenozoic era saw the evolution of the first primates resembling present-day tree-shrews? a. Miocene b. Paleocene c. Pleistocene d. Eocene
2. What is the characteristic feature that distinguishes Platyrrhini (New World Monkeys) from Catarrhini (Old World Monkeys)? a. Tail length b. Dentition c. Brain size d. Limb adaptation

3. Which feature is a distinguishing characteristic of Platyrrhini (New World Monkeys)? a. Narrow noses with closely placed nostrils b. Short, non-prehensile tails c. Long, prehensile tails d. Dentition with 32 teeth
4. Which of the following primates is classified under the suborder Prosimii? a. Gibbon b. Lemur c. Baboon d. Gorilla

B. Answer the following questions: 1. What is the dental formula for Catarrhini? 2. Compare the nasal structure and dental characteristics of Platyrrhini and Catarrhini. 3. Describe two similarities and two differences between apes and modern humans. 4. Explain the significance of the fossils of Dryopithecus and Ramapithecus in understanding human evolution. 5. Describe the main characteristic features of Australopithecus and its importance in human evolutionary history. 6. Discuss the key differences between Neanderthal Man and Cro-Magnon Man, highlighting their respective contributions to human evolution. 7. Trace the evolutionary lineage from Dryopithecus to Homo sapiens sapiens, detailing the major milestones and characteristic adaptations that occurred during this journey. 8. Compare and contrast Homo habilis and H. erectus in terms of their physical characteristics, behavior, and cultural advancements.
Project work Design an evolutionary tree of human evolution in a chart paper and label them using different colors.
